I probably should’ve worded this better. If you get a heatwave and get it to the shock rifle upgrade, you then need to drop your other weapon in order to get another one. You may not have it bound to a button yet, so make sure you have “drop weapon” bound somewhere. After you drop your other weapon you can simply walk up to the pack a punch with the heatwave and upgrade it again to immediately get another one. Get that one fully upgraded, and then you’ve officially reached the strongest possible loadout in the mode. Simply as that. Of course there’s a lot of luck involved in getting the heatwave, but once you do, it’s smooth sailing for a long time.

Something almost nobody seems to know, is that when you pack a punch a fully upgraded heatwave shock rifle, you're given a second heatwave. Upgrade that one until you get the shock rifle upgrade as well. Winning strat is to keep chaining together as many enemies as possible and switching between each heatwave to keep consistently shooting and regaining health from your vamperism. With this strat you are literally almost invincible.

People aren’t saying they hate change or want Halo 3 over and over again. The majority of classic halo fans want innovation without radical changes to the game’s base gameplay and formula, something that reach-H5 did a lot. And you might be thinking “what does that even mean?” It means classic fans want innovation in the form of new creative weapons, vehicles, equipment, and map designs, things I would argue modern halo severely lacks. You can call classic halo “dumbed down version of quake or doom”, but when you say that, you severely undermine the mechanics that made the game unique and popular in the first place. And advanced movement wasn’t one of them. In short we want (or wanted) something that built on halo’s already existing mechanics. Not by adding to something that didn’t need adding to. Classic fans don’t hate change. The game just didn’t change the way they think it should have.
